article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced hybrid
Genetics: Strawberry OG × Tiramisu
Breeder: The Cali Connection
THC Content: 23%
CBD Content: Typically below 1%
Terpene Profile: myrcene , beta-caryophyllene , limonene
Primary Flavors: Strawberry, sweet cream, vanilla, citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): 65–75 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: mid to late October
Indoor Yield: Medium
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Strawberry Tiramisu sounds like a strain engineered around a dessert menu, yet its ancestry gives the flower considerably more depth than simple sweetness. Fresh strawberry and cream occupy the most obvious aromatic layer, but beneath them sit lemony OG, earthy hash, vanilla, pastry, and the richer resinous character carried through Tiramisu. The Cali Connection created the hybrid by taking its Strawberry OG mother and pollinating it with a reversed Tiramisu selection, joining a fruit-heavy OG line with a Wedding Cake and Gelato 45 descendant. Mature plants combine a sturdy, productive frame with dense resinous flowers, while the finished cannabis moves between bright berry sweetness and a darker creamy-hash finish. It is an especially natural fit for growers who value terpene expression and extraction quality as much as raw flower production.
Genetics and Lineage

The maternal side of Strawberry Tiramisu is The Cali Connection’s Strawberry OG, officially listed as Bruce Banner #3 × SFV OG IBL. Bruce Banner #3 carries OG Kush and Strawberry Diesel influence, giving the plant strong potency, vigorous growth, sweet strawberry character, and a sharper diesel edge. SFV OG IBL reinforces lemon, earth, pine, resin, and classic Southern California OG structure. The resulting Strawberry OG became valued for its strawberry-lemon-pie aroma and combination of fruity sweetness with a more traditional OG backbone.

Tiramisu forms the pollen side of the cross and was reversed to produce feminized seed. Its pedigree is Wedding Cake × Gelato 45. Wedding Cake contributes creamy dough, pepper, earth, resin, and substantial potency through its Triangle Kush and Animal Mints -associated background. Gelato 45 comes from Sunset Sherbet × Thin Mint Cookies , adding sweet cream, fruit, mint, pastry, and another layer of dense trichome production. Combined in Tiramisu, those families produce vanilla, chocolate, buttery sweetness, and creamy hash rather than one-dimensional sugar.

Strawberry Tiramisu therefore brings together several influential California families—OG Kush, Strawberry Diesel, Cookies, Gelato, Wedding Cake, and SFV OG—without losing a recognizable sensory direction. Strawberry OG provides the brighter fruit and citrus, while Tiramisu deepens the cross with cream, hash, pastry, and dessert-like richness. The breeder’s goal was not merely to attach two attractive names to the same package; the structural qualities of both parents were also selected for solid production, cloning ability, and a plant that responds well to canopy shaping.
Effects and Experience

The experience generally begins on the more sociable side of the spectrum. A moderate amount can produce a pleasant lift in mood, greater interest in conversation, and a sense that music or visual entertainment deserves more attention than it did a few minutes earlier. The effect is not usually as sharp or restless as a pure Haze-style strain , nor does the body immediately become heavy. That makes the early portion suitable for relaxed social settings, creative hobbies, gaming, or an evening that has not yet reached the couch.

As the session develops, physical relaxation becomes more obvious. Tension may gradually leave the shoulders and limbs while the initial euphoria settles into a calmer mental state. This transition reflects the hybrid pedigree particularly well: Strawberry OG preserves enough brightness to keep the opening lively, while Wedding Cake, Gelato, and OG ancestry provide the weight that arrives later. Larger servings are more likely to emphasize body heaviness, appetite, and a quieter pace.

Exact potency depends on the plant and finished batch because The Cali Connection does not publish a fixed THC percentage for the line. Consumers should therefore pay more attention to laboratory testing on the actual flower than to universal strain claims. Strong examples can produce dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, mental haze, or temporary anxiety when overconsumed. The cultivar’s smooth strawberries-and-cream flavor may make it easy to underestimate how much has been consumed, so gradual dosing is sensible.
Medical Benefits

Strawberry Tiramisu may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who prefer a hybrid that does not move immediately toward sedation. The more upbeat beginning can make stress, low mood, or mental fatigue feel less dominant for some people, while the later physical phase may help muscular tension or persistent discomfort become less intrusive. That progression can be useful during the transition from daytime activity into evening rest, particularly for consumers who dislike marijuana that feels sleepy from the first inhalation.

Higher doses may produce more pronounced relaxation, appetite stimulation, and drowsiness as the experience matures. Those effects can make the cultivar more appropriate later in the day for many consumers, although response to high-THC cannabis differs substantially between individuals. People who are particularly sensitive to THC-related anxiety should remain cautious because an initially pleasant cerebral lift can become uncomfortable when the dose is pushed too far.

The breeder describes Strawberry Tiramisu as having a high and unusual terpene expression but does not provide one universal laboratory panel. Myrcene, beta-caryophyllene, and limonene are commonly associated with similar strawberry, OG, and dessert-oriented phenotypes and fit the strain’s fruit, citrus, earth, spice, and creamy-hash profile. Those aromatic compounds help explain the sensory character but should not be interpreted as evidence that the cultivar treats a particular medical condition. Batch-specific testing, personal tolerance, medications, and appropriate medical guidance remain more meaningful.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Fresh strawberry sits at the center of the bouquet. The aroma is closer to ripe fruit and strawberry cream than artificial candy, with a soft dairy-like sweetness contributed by Tiramisu. Citrus from Strawberry OG can brighten the top end, giving certain phenotypes a strawberry-lemon quality before the deeper dessert notes become obvious. The combination creates an aroma that feels fresh at first but grows noticeably richer as the flower is handled.

Grinding the buds releases the darker half of the profile. Hash, pastry, vanilla, mild earth, and occasional cocoa-like richness emerge beneath the berries, reflecting the Wedding Cake and Gelato 45 ancestry embedded inside Tiramisu. Strawberry OG adds a faint OG sharpness that prevents the flower from becoming overly sweet. Some plants may lean heavily toward strawberries and cream, while others emphasize hash, dough, and citrus with the fruit serving as a background accent.

On the palate, sweet strawberry commonly appears first, followed by cream and vanilla through the middle of the inhale. Citrus may briefly sharpen the flavor before the exhale settles into hash, pastry, and earth. Vaporization tends to preserve the strawberry and creamy top notes particularly well, while combustion pushes the resinous and earthy components forward. A controlled drying period and careful cure are especially important with this cultivar because the delicate fresh-fruit aromas are easier to lose than the heavier hash notes.
Growing Information

Strawberry Tiramisu was selected with practical cultivation traits in mind. The Cali Connection describes the plant as solid yielding, structurally impressive, easy to clone, and responsive to topping. Those characteristics make it suitable for growers who want to preserve a favored phenotype and repeat it across multiple cycles. Left mostly natural, plants can build a strong upright framework; topping shifts more energy toward lateral growth and creates a broader canopy with several productive leaders.

Indoor flowering requires approximately 65–75 days, giving the line a somewhat wider finishing window than Tiramisu itself. That range reflects phenotype variation and makes trichome maturity more useful than a calendar alone when deciding when to harvest. The breeder classifies yield as medium despite describing well-grown plants as capable of very respectable production, so it is better to think of Strawberry Tiramisu as a quality-oriented hybrid rather than a strain selected strictly for maximum grams per square meter. Lighting, vegetative time, root volume, training, and environmental control will all affect final weight.

Topping early in vegetative growth allows the plant enough time to recover and build strong lateral branches before flowering begins. Low-stress training can then spread those branches into a more even canopy, while a light trellis helps hold flowering sites in position as buds gain weight. Growers who find a particularly desirable strawberry-and-cream phenotype may appreciate the breeder’s emphasis on easy cloning, since keeping a mother allows that specific terpene expression to be reproduced rather than rediscovered from seed.

Dense, resinous flowers make airflow important during the final stages of bloom. Moderate humidity and consistent circulation around the canopy help prevent moisture from lingering between calyxes. The plant does not require extreme feeding simply because it has vigorous ancestry; stable irrigation, adequate drainage, and balanced nutrition provide a more reliable path to strong flower development. Growers should also avoid excessive late-flower manipulation that could bruise trichome-rich buds or disrupt ripening.

Outdoors, the 65–75-day flowering cycle generally requires favorable conditions well into October in many Northern Hemisphere gardens. Full sun, ample root space, and good drainage allow plants to develop substantially larger frameworks than indoors. Regions with prolonged dry autumn weather are especially well suited, while growers facing early rain may benefit from greenhouse protection or careful canopy management.

Extraction is one of the more interesting uses for the harvest. The Cali Connection specifically emphasizes Strawberry Tiramisu’s fragrant resin and distinctive terpene expression in concentrates. Well-selected plants can produce rosin, dry sift, or ice-water hash carrying a concentrated combination of strawberry, cream, hash, and citrus. For that purpose, preserving aroma through gentle harvesting, moderate drying temperatures, and careful storage may matter as much as maximizing flower weight.
FAQ
What strains make Strawberry Tiramisu?

The Cali Connection created Strawberry Tiramisu by crossing Strawberry OG with a reversed Tiramisu. Strawberry OG is officially listed as Bruce Banner #3 × SFV OG IBL, while Tiramisu is Wedding Cake × Gelato 45.
What does Strawberry Tiramisu taste like?

The main profile combines ripe strawberry, sweet cream, vanilla, citrus, hash, pastry, and mild earth. The breeder especially emphasizes strawberries and cream with a touch of hash, while individual phenotypes may lean more heavily toward fruit or dessert-like flavors.
Is Strawberry Tiramisu indica or sativa?

It is best described as a balanced hybrid. Its effects often begin upbeat, euphoric, and socially engaging before physical relaxation becomes stronger. Individual phenotypes and dosage can shift the experience toward either the more active Strawberry OG side or the heavier Tiramisu side.
How long does Strawberry Tiramisu take to flower?

The Cali Connection lists an indoor flowering period of approximately 65–75 days. Growers should use trichome maturity and flower development rather than relying entirely on the calendar because different plants within the seed line can finish at different points in that range.
Who bred Strawberry Tiramisu?

Strawberry Tiramisu was bred by The Cali Connection. It is sold as a feminized photoperiod cultivar and was created by reversing the breeder’s Tiramisu selection and using that pollen on its Strawberry OG mother.
Final Thoughts on Strawberry Tiramisu

Strawberry Tiramisu demonstrates how dessert-oriented cannabis can remain genetically and aromatically complex. Strawberry OG gives the hybrid ripe berry, lemon, OG structure, and a brighter mental edge, while Tiramisu introduces vanilla, cream, pastry, hash, and the resin-heavy influence of Wedding Cake and Gelato 45. Neither side completely dominates the finished flower.

The experience follows the same gradual layering. An initially upbeat, sociable high can fit creative or recreational activity, but deeper relaxation begins to take over as the session continues. Larger servings bring the heavier ancestry forward, making this weed strain increasingly appropriate for evening use.

Cultivators receive a plant that clones readily, responds well to topping, and finishes in approximately 65–75 days. Production is officially classified as medium, yet the breeder emphasizes sturdy structure and solid harvests. The greater attraction may be the resin itself, especially for growers interested in extracting the strawberry, cream, citrus, and hash profile into solventless concentrates.

For consumers looking for strawberry-flavored weed that offers more than candy sweetness, this hybrid provides a much broader spectrum. Fresh fruit introduces the experience, but vanilla, pastry, citrus, OG resin, and creamy hash give it lasting depth. That combination makes Strawberry Tiramisu a natural continuation of The Cali Connection’s dessert-focused breeding without reducing the plant to flavor alone.
